title: Meaningful colour and decorative colour: the difference

videos.script: Here is a bar chart with six bars, and six colours. Blue, red, green, purple, cyan, orange. {{six}} What does red mean? Nothing. The software gave each bar a colour because it could. The names are already on the axis. {{nothing}} But the reader does not know that. Colour is the first thing the eye reads, and every colour on a chart looks like it is saying something. Red looks like a warning. {{warning}} Now the same data with five grey bars and one strong one. Before you read a word, you know which bar matters. {{grey}} That is the difference this lesson is about. Meaningful colour carries information: a category, a value, the one thing to look at. Decorative colour carries nothing, and still costs the reader attention. {{difference}} You will learn to use colour once, on purpose, and to keep it consistent from one chart to the next. {{plan}}
